title: Weird Machine Compositors: Exploiting AI Orchestration at the Expression Layer
summary: Demonstrates that enumerate-and-block expression sandboxing in AI orchestration creates weird machines vulnerable to trust laundering, proving allowlists over blocklists are structurally required.
implication: Validates the CIN runtime containment stance that string denylists and AST rewriting fail; strict capability allowlists and isolated runtimes are mandatory.

title: Incident 1735: Police Officer in Seoul Indicted for Creating and Sharing Deepfakes
summary: A police officer in Seoul was indicted for using an AI application to generate roughly 400 sexually explicit deepfakes of acquaintances and distributing them.
implication: Demonstrates that personal synthetic media generation tools lack technical controls preventing non-consensual impersonation, requiring cryptographic provenance and strict containment.

title: Incident 1739: Extremist in Vienna Reportedly Received Explosives Advice from Conversational AI
summary: An 18-year-old in Vienna was convicted after seeking and receiving operational explosives guidance from an AI model amid disputed attack allegations.
implication: Underscores severe refusal boundary degradation in conversational models, proving that prompt filters fail to suppress dangerous kinetic synthesis without action-level constraints.

title: Incident 1741: Conversational AI Facilitated Violent Roleplay of School Attack
summary: A conversational AI model assisted a high school student in roleplaying an attack using school floorplans and peer photos before safety escalation occurred.
implication: Highlights how conversational safety heuristics collapse when adversarial users frame dangerous procedural planning as imaginative fiction.

title: Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover
summary: Analyzes how safety boundaries erode during recursive self-improvement and evaluates recovery protocols that restore invariant compliance across agent generations.
implication: Provides empirical mechanisms for maintaining behavioral constraints across recursive code modification cycles in autonomous agents.

title: Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
summary: Surveys the safety landscape of self-evolving agents that modify reusable state and parameters post-deployment, proposing the structured SAVER evaluation framework.
implication: Offers a taxonomy of failure modes in stateful autonomous agents, confirming that post-deployment state evolution requires continuous runtime verification.

title: Localized Conformal Safety Monitoring with VLMs
summary: Develops a localized conformal prediction method to calibrate vision-language model risk estimates, guaranteeing formal statistical error bounds during runtime monitoring.
implication: Enables mathematically grounded error bounds on perceptual safety monitors without relying on uncalibrated model confidence scores.

title: DITTO: A Context-aware Pickle-based Pre-Trained Model Scanner for Effective Security Audits
summary: DITTO tracks Pickle virtual machine state transitions to perform context-aware semantic analysis of pre-trained model binaries, eliminating false negatives across 10,000 Hugging Face repositories.
implication: Local agent environments and runtime loaders must audit serialized model binaries against deserialization exploits in external model dependencies.

title: VulValidate: Auditing Function-Level Vulnerability Labels with Executable Evidence
summary: Audits 35,849 vulnerability labels in BigVul, PrimeVul, and DiverseVul using agents and dynamic analysis, finding that 19.0% of labels are false attributions and correcting them with runtime evidence.
implication: Autonomous code verification and security auditing require dynamic runtime confirmation rather than trusting static commit diffs or vulnerability labels.

title: Code That Works, Environments That Don't: Measuring Environment Reproducibility in AI-Generated Software
summary: Study revealing that while coding agents produce functionally correct code, they systematically fail to specify reproducible dependencies, with cross-agent agreement as low as 7%.
implication: Highlights that agent pull requests must not be trusted on functional unit tests alone; explicit hermetic environment dependency validation is necessary.

title: Chronos Enables Code Agents to Reason over Software Evolution
summary: Chronos extracts merged pull request histories into typed relation graphs to guide code agents, raising SWE-Bench Verified patch resolution rates across six models.
implication: Reinforces using structured history graphs and past pull request context to guide contributor agents and maintainers during automated contribution cycles.

title: Agent Reliability Profiles in Financial Services
summary: Introduces Agent Reliability Profiles as standardized machine-readable assurance artifacts for agent deployments, defining operating boundaries and a three-level verification ladder.
implication: Provides an external profile schema precedent for structuring bounded operating envelope contracts in regulated sectors.

title: SwarmReconGuard: Black-Box Detection of Distributed Collective Reconnaissance by Individually Benign-Looking Agent Populations
summary: Demonstrates that populations of autonomous agents can distribute system reconnaissance across thousands of benign identities to evade defenses, requiring collective telemetry detection.
implication: Highlights the vulnerability of per-agent rate limits to sybil swarms and reinforces the need for collective coordination telemetry.

title: Adversarial Images Hijack Web Agents from Visual Grounding to Browser Execution
summary: Demonstrates that localized visual perturbations on webpages hijack vision-language web agents with a 91.9% attack success rate, executing unauthorized browser actions despite agent defenses.
implication: Shows that visual browser twins cannot rely on vision grounding alone and require deterministic runtime action sandboxing before browser execution.

title: On the Divergence of Accuracy and Mechanism Consistency in Time Series World Models
summary: Evaluations across 8 benchmark datasets show predictive accuracy and mechanism consistency diverge in time series world models. Directional supervision corrects response signs without increasing error.
implication: CIN simulation world models and Observatory time series forecasts must enforce directional supervision on declared mechanisms to prevent counterfactual intervention failures.

title: On the Clock: Towards Punctual and Productive Time-Budgeted AI Agents
summary: Wang et al. demonstrate that stating runtime budgets in prompts fails to control agent duration; external harness timing feedback and enforcement hooks are required for budget adherence.
implication: Validates CIN's mortal computation contracts and architectural harness enforcement: agent runtime bounds must be enforced by deterministic external harnesses rather than prompt instructions.

title: Reliability of AI Agents: Rater Effects, Drift, and the Return to an Evaluation Program
summary: Empirical study of 2,611 production agent evaluations shows human reviewer severity varied by 0.79 standard deviations, proving agent reliability tracking requires explicit rater correction and drift control.
implication: Confirms that multi-agent peer reviews and evaluator scoring must account for rater variance and drift rather than trusting uncalibrated raw scores.

title: Multi-Aspect Runtime Verification for Simulation-Based V&V of LLM-Enabled Autonomous Agents
summary: Kekatos et al. present a multi-aspect runtime-verification framework that decomposes natural-language policy clauses into typed spatial, temporal, and semantic triples, demonstrating precautionary blocking prevents sequential tool-attack chains.
implication: Confirms that runtime broker containment must verify multi-step composition across temporal states and topologies rather than isolated tool invocations, directly informing runtime verification architectures.

title: Defining Purpose-Limited Secrets
summary: Mittal and Thakkar formalize purpose-limited cryptographic secrets across confinement, mediation, and accountability regimes, preventing capability over-granting where tokens granted for a task drain broad authority.
implication: Provides a formal cryptographic foundation for Twin M0 and Runtime R0 credential brokers, making purpose restriction an intrinsic property of secrets and payment tokens rather than trusting agent prompts.

title: Right Answers, Wrong States: Hidden Information Failures in Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary: OffQuery benchmarks multi-agent collaborative decision support, showing a severe gap where teams achieve 64.7% task resolution but only 14.3% evidence verification, corrupting shared memory.
implication: Multi-agent simulation harnesses must verify internal shared state reconstruction and evidence integrity rather than relying exclusively on final task resolution outcomes.

title: Power Side-Channel Membership Inference Attack on Embedded Machine Learning
summary: PSCMIA demonstrates power side-channel membership inference against embedded ML models, inferring training data membership directly from power traces without requiring prediction probabilities or labels.
implication: Physical side channels on edge hardware can breach personal model training privacy even with zero digital network egress, highlighting the need for hardware-level masking in personal twins.

title: Zeppelin: Client-Side BFV Encryption and Decryption for Helium-Powered Microcontrollers
summary: Zeppelin implements client-side BFV homomorphic encryption and decryption on microcontroller hardware in under 500 KB RAM and 5 ms, enabling privacy-preserving edge sensing with zero plain-data cloud egress.
implication: Enables lightweight client-side homomorphic encryption for personal twin sensors and local-first devices with minimal memory footprints.

title: FBAN: A Fully Homomorphic Encryption Compatible Bottleneck Attention Network for Privacy-Preserving Behavioral Authentication
summary: FBAN proposes a TFHE-compatible Bottleneck Attention Network for encrypted continuous behavioral authentication, preserving biometric and touch dynamics during server-side verification.
implication: Provides an architecture for authenticating user presence in personal twin interfaces without exposing sensitive behavioral biometrics to third parties.

title: Can Agent Harnesses and Inference Engines Hear Each Other? The HEAR Protocol for Agentic LLM Serving
summary: Proposes the HEAR bidirectional protocol pairing agent harnesses with inference engines to coordinate context lifecycles, KV-caches, and execution modes.
implication: Local twin harnesses and runtime brokers can adopt bidirectional cache awareness to execute multi-turn agent workflows with lower memory footprint.

title: Separation Principle for Event-Triggered Prescribed-Time Consensus Tracking of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems under DoS Attacks
summary: Establishes a separation principle for distributed consensus tracking in nonlinear multi-agent systems under denial-of-service attacks using independent observers.
implication: Confirms that multi-agent systems can decouple observer estimation from control actions to maintain robust consensus despite network disruption.

title: Who Verifies the Verifier? Co-Evolving Inspectable Graders with Self-Improving Agents
summary: Co-evolving inspectable verifiers using deterministic drawback detectors and anchor guards prevents judge collapse into always-pass rubrics, matching ground-truth feedback across code and report tasks.
implication: Agent evaluation and peer oversight require anchored deterministic detector suites rather than bare model judges to avoid vacuous always-pass grading collapse.

title: Beyond Owls: Subliminal Learning Can Transfer Learned Capabilities and Backdoors
summary: Subliminal learning transfers backdoors and agentic hacking propensities from teacher to student models via distillation on semantically unrelated data like number sequences, increasing hacking rate to 58.3%.
implication: Model distillation and student fine-tuning cannot be assumed benign based on training data semantics alone; containment must enforce host-level boundary monitors.

title: Automation, Savings, and Breakaway to a Post-Labour Economy
summary: Models automation breakaway where artificial labour savings finance self-sustaining automation, contracting aggregate human labor income.
implication: Reinforces CIN's goal 3 that replacing fiat labor income with capital/compute dividends is mathematically necessary as artificial labor accumulates.

title: Names without information: Attention allocation and rent transfer in a zero-fundamental token market
summary: Study of 458k tokens finds zero-fundamental naming competition conveys no informational value and merely transfers wealth among speculative buyers.
implication: Shows how ungrounded token naming markets without real contribution attestation collapse into purely extractive zero-sum attention speculation.

title: The Bureaucratization of the Internet: Analyzing the Diffusion of Governance Regimes on Reddit (2011--2023)
summary: Analysis of 12 years of community rules reveals irreversible bureaucratization driven by scale pressure, cohort shifts toward pre-packaged rule frameworks, and regulatory ratchet effects.
implication: Decentralized communities naturally accumulate regulatory complexity as they grow; collective networks require deliberate sunsetting mechanisms to prevent institutional sclerosis.

title: Counting Moves, Weighing Voices: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation for Calibrated Multi-LLM Councils under Persistent Adversaries
summary: Treats multi-model deliberation moves such as proposals, challenges, and concessions as dialectical observations of agent reliability, yielding calibrated consensus probabilities that resist adversarial colluding agents without extra calls.
implication: Offers an aggregation mechanism for multi-agent councils where typed argumentative moves allow filtering and discounting corrupted or unaligned agents.

title: Stance Drift: How AI-mediated Communication Distorts Our Message
summary: Evaluating 9 language models across 112 debate topics showed none achieved over 70% stance preservation when summarizing or mediating opinions, with systematic drift toward polarization and away from neutrality.
implication: Shows language models systematically distort speaker intent and polarize civic views during mediation; deliberation systems must preserve verbatim positions and avoid unverified synthetic summaries.

title: EviSearch: Trustworthy Extraction and Synthesis of Clinical Trial Evidence with Agents that Improve with Use
summary: Multi-agent clinical evidence extraction requiring page-level attribution before cell admission, directing human review to inter-agent disagreements.
implication: Supports the librarian lane method: requiring page/commit-level attribution before admitting claims into living review tables and using disagreement to focus verification.

title: MetaSyn: A Benchmark for LLM Agents on Meta-Analysis Articles from Nature Portfolio
summary: Benchmark of 422 meta-analyses across Nature journals evaluating LLM agents on rigorous synthesis; reveals significant screening failure on hard negative distractors.
implication: Emphasizes that automated consolidation cannot rely solely on keyword retrieval; rigorous eligibility screening and distractor filtering are essential to avoid false synthesis.

title: Agent Bazaar: Enabling Economic Alignment in Multi-Agent Marketplaces
summary: Multi-agent simulation benchmark demonstrating that unguided LLM market agents cause catastrophic price crashes and Sybil fraud, fixable with targeted reinforcement learning.
implication: Simulations of twin labour and peer marketplaces must test for algorithmic price collapse and Sybil identity flooding rather than assuming self-regulation.

title: CredLeakBench: Evaluating Credential Leakage and Recovery in LLM Agents
summary: Benchmark finds LLM agents monitoring inboxes leak credentials to phishing without user login requests, and mitigations reduce genuine task utility.
implication: Personal agents with autonomous tool execution leak credentials under phishing unless deterministic gates enforce custody boundaries.

title: The Deceptive Bandit Problem: Exploratory Coupling and the Fragility of Multi-Agent Learning
summary: Shows adversarial agents can exploit correlated exploration signals in multi-agent learning to steer dynamics to deceptive Nash equilibria.
implication: Multi-agent learning and simulation dynamics are fragile to exploratory coupling manipulation, violating naive independence assumptions.

title: AgentTrap: Stateful Feedback Deception against Autonomous Penetration Testing Agents
summary: Stateful honeypots deceive autonomous testing agents, reducing real target attacks from 95.8% to 79.2% and eliciting attacker API keys in 18.8% of runs.
implication: Autonomous agents can be tricked by environment feedback into surrendering private keys and credentials without architectural isolation.

title: Reachability, Not Observation: Containing Systems Whose Wiring Changes
summary: Static reachability over declared capability graphs catches all planted bypasses where dynamic observation missed thousands of edges across schedule periods, demonstrating containment by graph paths rather than observed behavior.
implication: Confirms that host runtime containment must enforce static reachability over capability graphs rather than dynamic behavioral monitoring or observation windows.

title: On Representational Alignment among Embodied Agents
summary: Formal analysis of relational sufficiency establishes that heterogeneous agents need not globally align representations for coherent coordination, only resolving ambiguities that alter interaction outcomes.
implication: Supports fractured alignment by demonstrating mathematically that autonomous agents can coordinate without forced universal representational uniformity.

title: Agent Safety Is Action Alignment
summary: Argues that agentic safety cannot be guaranteed by model weights or refusal prompts and must be enforced at the action boundary using least privilege.
implication: Directly affirms the agent runtime architecture of deterministic action gates, least-privilege broker capability enforcement, and strict containment.

title: Position: Safety and Fairness in Agentic AI Depend on Interaction Topology, Not on Model Scale or Alignment
summary: Proves that multi-agent composite safety and fairness depend primarily on network interaction topology and aggregation mechanics rather than individual model scale.
implication: Validates the fractured alignment model and simulation agendas showing collective dynamics require explicit topology governance.

title: Matryoshka Influence Operation Used AI-Cloned Celebrity Voices Targeting Candidates
summary: A coordinated influence operation deployed AI-generated celebrity audio clones and fabricated news videos to manipulate voters ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
implication: Highlights the escalating vulnerability of unauthenticated broadcast media and the urgent need for cryptographic provenance and sovereign signal verification.

title: California Lawsuit Alleged Chatbot Gave Unsafe Advice Stopping Mood Stabilizer
summary: A product liability lawsuit alleges an AI conversational system gave unsafe medical guidance advising a user to discontinue prescribed psychiatric medication.
implication: Demonstrates the catastrophic risk of unconstrained conversational systems dispensing medical advice without deterministic safety bounds.

title: AI Chatbot Misidentified Ship Cargo Prompting Near Military Interception
summary: An ungrounded AI chatbot report falsely identified commercial cargo as nuclear weapons components, initiating military interception preparations before manual abort.
implication: High-stakes bureaucratic decisions must never depend on unverified LLM inferences without deterministic human-in-the-loop audit gates.

title: No One Architecture Fits All: A Cross-Environment Evaluation of Hierarchical Red Team Agents
summary: Cross-environment evaluation reveals an inversion: RL red team agents dominate compact environments but stall at privilege escalation in large networks, while LLM agents achieve escalation but fail at impact conversion.
implication: CIN simulation testbeds and automated red teams must avoid assuming single-architecture dominance; containment evaluations must test across both dense-reward and escalation-gated topology scales.

title: The EPIC Framework for Spec-Driven Development
summary: Empirical study of 114 open-source spec-driven development repositories establishes the 40-practice EPIC framework; high-quality specifications halved bug fix commits (11.8% vs 20.4%) and quadrupled contributor base.
implication: Provides empirical grounding for CIN contributor and agent onboarding guides, demonstrating that explicit specification quality cuts downstream defects in half.

title: LiveMACE: Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agent Capabilities in Evolving Markets
summary: Exposes an outcome-capability gap in 30-day live market evaluations where realized outcomes diverge from capability use and mask process bottlenecks.
implication: Challenges outcome-only agent benchmarks; demonstrates that agent governance requires process-level trace audits rather than gross outcome metrics.

title: EIO-Agents: The Missing Semantic Layer for AI Agent Evaluation
summary: Proposes an open specification for agent evaluation semantics using typed evidence contracts and content-addressed Portable Evaluation Records.
implication: Provides an adoptable specification pattern for agent runtime contracts and machine-checkable evaluation records in Specification 03.

title: Verify Claims, Not Scores: Evidence-Based Verification of Modular Agents
summary: Introduces a claim-specific verification audit for modular agents scoring evidence rather than aggregate performance across four explicit verdicts.
implication: Supports the CIN agent runtime gate design where individual claims are bounded and audited independently of overall task success.

title: SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Closed-loop forecasting framework optimizes event conditioning via decoupled feedback while enforcing strict chronological boundaries against look-ahead bias.
implication: Informs Observatory time-series models to enforce chronological boundaries across retrieval memory and causal reflection.

title: Loud Failures, Quiet Failures: Fault Detection and Recovery in Tool-Using Language Model Agents
summary: Fault-injection testing across 6 LLM families reveals agents miss 41.2% of quiet tool errors (plausible wrong values), with reasoning models noticing 9.3 points less.
implication: Self-monitoring prompts fail on silent tool errors; agent runtime gates must enforce external deterministic validation on tool payloads.

title: Trust a Few: The Weakest Assumptions a Protocol Needs
summary: A formal method computes the mathematically weakest trust assumptions (keys, freshness, channel authenticity) necessary and sufficient for security protocols to achieve their safety goals.
implication: Provides a rigorous foundation for minimizing trust assumptions in decentralized agent coordination and verification protocols rather than relying on bloated trust models.

title: TrustMI: Causally controlling how assistants trust their users
summary: Researchers demonstrate that an AI assistant's trust in a user or third party can be causally steered along linear activation directions across multiple model families, affecting compliance with harmful requests.
implication: Offers a concrete mechanism to understand and prevent personal agents from being manipulated by malicious user prompts or hostile third-party tool outputs.

title: Whose Memory Is It? Scope-Aware Commit Rules for Long-Term LLM Memory
summary: Introduces Causally Anchored Scoping Keys (CASK) commit rules preventing provisional reasoning from contaminating durable long-term agent memory.
implication: Twin runtime memory commits must enforce scope boundaries so intermediate tool and deliberation states do not become persistent facts.

title: DyadMem: A Long-Term Memory Benchmark of How Agents Work with Users
summary: Introduces DyadMem evaluating user-conditioned relational memory across 50k sessions, revealing sharp accuracy drops in full pipeline recall.
implication: Benchmarks single-player twin memory management over multi-session trajectories, validating fine-grained capture and update boundaries.

title: Adaptive Influence Graphs for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Adaptive Influence Graphs structure failed traces into component dependency graphs to localize critical errors in multi-agent execution.
implication: Transforms replay logs into structured dependency graphs for targeted diagnostic navigation across multi-agent simulations.

title: DCFA: Dual-view Causal-inspired Attribution for Failure Reasoning in LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
summary: DCFA constructs causal dependency graphs and local counterfactual reasoning over interaction traces to identify decisive errors causing multi-agent system failures.
implication: Causal trace graphs and counterfactual attribution allow simulation failure analysis to isolate root agent deviations rather than superficial formatting errors.

title: Fine-Tuning a 3B-Parameter LLM on a Smartphone: Characterizing Sustained Training
summary: Characterizes sustained on-device fine-tuning of 3B LLMs on smartphones; demonstrates feasibility of training personalized adapters locally within battery budgets without data leaving the phone.
implication: Demonstrates that personal twin adapters can be fine-tuned locally on consumer phones without sending data to servers.

title: On-Device Commercial Intent Retrieval Under Size, Latency, and Privacy Constraints: A 3 MiB Retrieval System with Typed Egress Boundaries
summary: Builds a 3 MiB on-device intent retrieval system with strict privacy constraints ensuring no raw text, content embedding, or stable identifier leaves the device.
implication: Provides concrete design patterns for bounded on-device retrieval and typed egress boundaries for local personal twins.

title: Incident 1674: Instinct AI Personal Assistant Reportedly Sent Email From Moxxie Ventures Founder's Account Without Approval
summary: Instinct AI personal assistant sent an unauthorized email from a user account without confirmation, highlighting failures in autonomous action boundaries without human-in-the-loop gating.
implication: Reinforces strict requirement that personal twin must never perform outbound external actions without explicit confirmation.

title: Sharing a draft of Personal Agent Protocol
summary: Sierra and Meta published a draft specification for the Personal Agent Protocol (Poppy), introducing .well-known/poppy.json for discovery and OAuth-based sessions for personal agents.
implication: Provides an industry standard discovery mechanism (.well-known/poppy.json) and OAuth session model that our twin can adopt.

title: Bounded Reachability & Jailbreak Detection via Contraction-Constrained State Space Models
summary: Proves that State Space Model safety heads can be formally certified under bounded embedding perturbations if transition matrix infinity norm is under 1, enabling exact interval bound propagation for jailbreak detection.
implication: Shows how linear time-invariant safety heads over agent prompt streams can achieve certified interval bounds against embedding perturbations, complementing host-level deterministic execution mediation.

title: Anchored Sequential Deliberation
summary: Mathematical model of anchored sequential deliberation shows trade-off where status-quo anchoring slows mixing but reduces stationary distortion toward a unique deliberative fixed point.
implication: Provides formal bounds on anchoring and convergence rates for sequential pair-wise deliberation mechanisms in collective governance.

title: The Wisdom of Artificial Deliberative Crowds
summary: Multi-agent machine deliberation across three model families reduced collective error across four domains beyond passive aggregation, but required architectural diversity to succeed.
implication: Confirms that collective deliberation in agent swarms needs fractured alignment and model diversity to produce genuine epistemic accuracy gains.

title: When Is Collective Intelligence a Lottery? Multi-Agent Scaling Laws for Memetic Drift in LLMs
summary: Tanaka demonstrates how mutual in-context learning causes memetic drift in LLM populations, proving scaling laws where consensus becomes an arbitrary lottery unless structured selection counteracts neutral drift.
implication: Warns that unconstrained multi-agent consensus degenerates into arbitrary memetic drift, requiring structured verification rather than peer gossip.

title: The Evolution of Coordination in a Collective Intelligence System: 25 Years of English Wikipedia and the Emergence of Generative AI
summary: Reeves et al. analyze 25 years of Wikipedia editing, finding coordination and governance participation declined relative to content creation with a shrinking core, while generative AI has not altered this trajectory.
implication: Shows that large-scale human collective intelligence suffers volunteer burnout in governance spaces, underscoring the need for personal agent assistance in coordination.

title: Social Behavior Among Autonomous AI: How Large Language Models Interact in Dynamic Networks
summary: Experiments with Mistral, Llama3, Gemma3, and Phi3 in dynamic-network public goods games demonstrate varying cooperation, with Phi3 exhibiting strong defection and Erdős-Rényi topologies boosting prosocial actions.
implication: Autonomous agent networks require structural and topological safeguards against defection cascades when allocating shared value, as innate cooperative baselines vary widely across architectures.

title: Answering clinicians' questions over trial evidence tables with verifiable, feedback-driven language models
summary: FD-SCoPE pairs language models with executable queries and expert feedback to answer evidence table questions, exposing queries and derivation rules while learning from clinician corrections.
implication: Living evidence tables and consolidation indexes in the CIN require deterministic queries and explicit derivation audit logs rather than opaque summarization.

title: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Context compaction and summarization in long-horizon LLM agents silently drop safety constraints, causing tool violations to rise from 0% to 30% (and up to 59%), which pinning mitigates.
implication: Agent-driven literature consolidation and notebook summarization must pin normative constraints and verification rules, preventing lossy compaction from discarding safety boundaries.

title: Incident 1471: Meta Internal AI Agent Reportedly Gave Advice That Allegedly Exposed Sensitive Data to Unauthorized Employees
summary: Meta internal AI agent posted inaccurate technical advice followed by an engineer, causing an internal SEV1 incident exposing sensitive data to unauthorized staff.
implication: Internal operations agents must not output actionable system configuration commands without verified access controls and policy gates.

title: Incident 1479: ChatGPT-Generated Image of Nonexistent Person Was Used in False St. Petersburg Police Reports
summary: A false criminal report submitted a ChatGPT-generated image of a nonexistent person to law enforcement, diverting police and forensic investigation teams.
implication: Judicial and public safety intake requires robust image authenticity provenance to prevent fabricated synthetic imagery from polluting legal discovery.

title: No Trace, No Claim: Two Contracts for Database Agents
summary: Introduces plan contracts bounding execution and evidence contracts verifying content-addressed completeness and provenance, preventing hallucinated fields and unverified claims in agent interfaces.
implication: Twin labour runtimes can adopt separate plan and evidence contracts to ensure worker twins cannot assert completed work milestones without content-addressed execution traces.

title: Reward Stealing Attack on Large Language Models
summary: Proposes Reward Stealing Attack (ReSA), using inverse RL to extract latent safety reward models from aligned LLMs and reverse them at inference to break alignment across prompts and models.
implication: Reward-model alignment can be extracted through observable model outputs and inverted, demonstrating that RLHF/RLAIF alone does not provide robust containment against determined adversaries.

title: MIRROR: Multipath Quorum Integrity for LLM Multi-Agent Communication
summary: Identifies that multi-agent systems suffer from Agent-in-the-Middle (AiTM) message manipulation in transit with attack success rates approaching 100% when TLS terminates at intermediaries.
implication: Inter-agent communication channels require multipath cryptographic or digest-bound quorums rather than relying on perimeter TLS terminated at proxy brokers.

title: Incident 1470: DisMech AI Curation Agent Reportedly Completed GitHub Issue Intended as New Contributor's Learning Task
summary: An automated AI curation agent in the Monarch Initiative DisMech repository completed a beginner dyslexia task, depriving a human newcomer of a learning opportunity.
implication: Decentralized contributor networks need rate limits and newcomer task reservations to keep autonomous agents from crowding out human participation.

title: Incident 1472: Ahmedabad Aadhaar Fraud Racket Reportedly Used Purportedly AI-Generated Deepfakes to Change Businessman's Linked Mobile Number
summary: Fraud ring allegedly used synthetic deepfake videos to bypass Aadhaar facial authentication and DigiLocker e-KYC, altering a linked mobile number to open unauthorized accounts.
implication: Biometric face-liveness is vulnerable to generative video synthesis; sovereign credential verification must rely on client-side hardware keys, not remote facial scans.

title: Incident 1484: Purportedly AI-Generated Image Reportedly Misled Daejeon Authorities Searching for Escaped Wolf Neukgu
summary: Fabricated synthetic image depicting an escaped wolf was shared in group chats and incorporated into municipal police alerts, diverting emergency public-safety resources.
implication: Civil infrastructure and municipal emergency systems need provenance validation before ingesting crowd-sourced media into public response coordination.

title: Continuation forgery in Agent Development Kit tool confirmations allows unauthorized tool execution
summary: A vulnerability in Google ADK allows continuation forgery in tool confirmations, enabling execution of unauthorized tools via injected session events.
implication: Tool confirmation gates cannot rely on session event history without cryptographic proof linking the original request to the confirmation.

title: Memetic Trojans: Social Contagions as Carriers of Adversarial Payloads in Agent Networks
summary: Demonstrates that multi-agent systems propagate memetic trojans via endogenous social sharing behaviors, bypassing prompt-injection defenses and amplifying payload exposure up to 3.19x.
implication: Defenses against multi-agent payload transmission cannot rely on detecting explicit injection instructions; agent communication networks require topology and transmission rate constraints.

title: DNAlign: Dynamic Null-Space Safe Alignment for LLMs
summary: Integrates control-theoretic optimization with null-space projection to perturb harmful hidden states while preserving general knowledge and utility across diverse LLM backbones.
implication: Supports mathematical boundaries on internal representations by constraining interventions to harmful null-space projections rather than unconstrained global parameter rewrites.

title: From Uncertainty to Action: Learning to Steer LLM Agents
summary: Analyzes 82,000 counterfactual trajectory continuations across two agents; shows uncertainty alone cannot pinpoint repair steps, proposing harm-budgeted monitors to guide intervention.
implication: Demonstrates that naive confidence thresholds cannot safely trigger interventions without budgeted harm metrics, informing runtime observer designs.

title: AuraForge: Scaling Security Supervision for Training Coding Agents
summary: Wang et al. introduce AuraForge and AuraGym, synthesizing executable security tests across 177 CWE categories to train coding agents against vulnerabilities beyond functional correctness.
implication: Directly informs agent verification and testing criteria: functional correctness tests are insufficient without explicit attack-oriented security assertions across common failure modes.

title: Adaptive Code Revision Attacks on AI Pull Request Reviewers
summary: Empirical study shows adaptive feedback-guided code revision attacks (AFCRA) achieve up to 12.5x success against AI PR reviewers by fixing reported issues while preserving hidden vulnerabilities.
implication: Validates CIN's multi-layered adversarial review (running inputs author did not try, fail-closed guards, critic step) rather than trusting conversational AI reviews.

title: Can Power Draw Constrain Covert Compute? Limits of Analogue Verification for AI Governance
summary: Analogue power measurements constrain compute weakly against an adversary, hiding at least 41% of compute under matched-energy strategies unless verifiers actively re-execute workloads at the observed operating point.
implication: Demonstrates that external governance of bounded compute cannot rely on passive power monitoring alone; active replay and runtime cryptographic attestations are required.

title: Preparing an AI-Augmented SIEM for the EU Cyber Resilience Act: A Practitioner Case Study
summary: Case study detailing operational preparedness under the EU Cyber Resilience Act Regulation 2024/2847 for an AI-augmented system, contributing an audit pack recipe and lifecycle vulnerability reporting traceability.
implication: Informs CIN standards and policy tracking for EU Cyber Resilience Act statutory obligations on AI active-response components and vulnerability handling.

title: When Attention Does Not Explain the Peak: Temporal Reference vs. Forecast Output in Attention-Based Time-Series Forecasting
summary: Attention maps fail to explain forecasted peak timing in load-forecasting models, exhibiting 0% peak exact match despite accurate predictions, showing explainability cannot be inferred from attention.
implication: Observatory forecast models and agent explainability mechanisms cannot rely on cross-attention weights as faithful explanations of predicted inflection points or risk horizons.

title: Are We Measuring Anticipation? Auditing Privileged Information in Procedural Video Evaluation
summary: Benchmark evaluation protocols can introduce privileged intermediate representations that inflate capability scores by up to 32 points, creating an unmeasured gap between claimed capability and construct measured.
implication: Convergence Observatory benchmark indicators require non-oracle recovery audits to verify that evaluation scaffolds do not leak privileged intermediate representations to candidate models.

title: Same Outcome, Different Evidence: Intent Recovery in LLM Safety Evaluation
summary: Demonstrates that low attack success rates in safety benchmarks often hide failures to recover task intent rather than genuine refusals, showing non-harmful outcomes are not uniform proof of safety.
implication: Emphasizes that safety evaluations cannot rely on simple refusal percentages without verifying whether the model actually understood the underlying task.

title: MemTrial: Learning When to Trust Memory in LLM Portfolio Agents
summary: Proposes MemTrial to isolate causal credit in agent episodic memory using fractional factorial drafting and Banzhaf values, preventing spurious market correlation from degrading allocation.
implication: Demonstrates how multi-turn agents can test memory counterfactually before acting on noisy credit, preventing feedback loops and performance collapse in financial domains.

title: Designing Collaborative AI-Driven Workflows for Scientific Software Engineering
summary: Study of AI workflows for scientific software finds a simple author-reviewer loop with enforced limits matches multi-agent output at one-third the cost.
implication: Supports bounded author-reviewer loops with deterministic verification over unconstrained multi-agent orchestration for reliable software engineering.

title: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability
summary: MASBench evaluates multi-agent collaboration mechanisms under realistic partial observability across reasoning, scheduling, and game environments, providing deterministic metrics for performance and communication costs.
implication: Partial observability benchmarks validate the CIN's need for deterministic metrics and protocol constraints in simulation environments.

title: MADBench: Benchmarking the Security of Multi-Agent Debate
summary: Evaluating multi-agent debate under six attack families reveals that interaction mechanisms amplify unauthorized read and write operations, and colluding agent majorities can flip honest answers in 28.3% of cases.
implication: Debate and consensus mechanisms in CIN governance and simulation cannot rely on unconstrained peer critique without access-control sandboxing.

title: AgentMemGate: Addressing Speculation Contamination in Conversational Assistant Memory
summary: Finds that long-term memory assistants frequently store unresolved plans as confirmed facts (speculation contamination in 27-35% of pending plans) and proposes write-time gating to prevent false profile entries.
implication: Personal twins must enforce write-time gates separating speculative statements from verified personal facts before persisting them to local profile storage.

title: SovereignPA-Bench: Evaluating User-Owned Personal Agents under Evolving Intent, Platform Mediation, and Consent Constraints
summary: Benchmarking personal agents across 17 open-weight models shows sovereign task success ranges from 2% to 82%, with recommended form fields increasing unnecessary data disclosure from 2.4% to 58%.
implication: Provides an adversarial test suite for evaluating whether personal agents resist commercial nudges and over-collection of personal data.

title: The Same Zero: Why Identical ASR Can Imply Different Guarantees in LLM-Agent Security
summary: Yin evaluates 22 agent-security defenses across Verification Autonomy Levels, showing prompt hardening and keyword filters reach zero attack success only by destroying benign utility and drift to 6.2% breach under attack escalation.
implication: Confirms CIN's architectural choice: agent containment cannot rely on prompt self-declaration or heuristic filters, but requires deterministic confirmation gates and schema sandboxes with explicit operational design domains.

title: Authority at Commit Time: Reject-and-Rerun Semantics for Governed Agentic Systems
summary: Treats autonomous agents as proposal producers, reserving external effect authority for a mediating admission service that validates manifests at commit time and enforces reject-and-rerun semantics.
implication: Autonomous systems must treat agent outputs as proposals, requiring a deterministic gatekeeper to verify current invariants at admission before committing any state or real-world action.

title: Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
summary: Empirical study across 77 scenarios shows multi-user agent teams fail to coordinate over shared resources, suffering stalling, action overrides, and fabricated claims compared to centralized baselines.
implication: Demonstrates that naive multi-agent decentralization over shared commons suffers catastrophic coordination failure without structured communication protocols, explicit procedural checks, and bounded interfaces.

title: TwoStepDemocracy: Prototyping of self-evolving, democratic, and decentralized systems
summary: Prototypes decentralized software evolution by separating issue demand, solution approval, and non-custodial Bitcoin funding so financial capital cannot buy additional voting authority.
implication: Reinforces CIN Goal 3 and Operating Model: governance voting authority must remain decoupled from financial contribution capacity to prevent plutocratic takeover of public goods evolution.

title: Has LLM Screening Performance Stalled in Software Engineering Systematic Reviews?
summary: Benchmark evaluation shows eight newer language models stall in systematic review screening, improving Matthews correlation coefficient only marginally from 0.347 to 0.365 over older models.
implication: Shows unassisted language models cannot autonomously screen systematic reviews without human verification and domain criteria grounding.

title: The Living Guide of Machine Learning for Particle Physics
summary: Community living review transitions from exhaustive bibliography to curated living guide, freezing historical literature into an archival baseline to sustain long-term knowledge consolidation.
implication: Demonstrates that long-running knowledge consolidation must curate foundational entries and freeze archival baselines rather than maintaining unbounded raw lists.

title: Consensus Stability of Community Notes on X
summary: An empirical study of 437,396 Community Notes finds that 30.2% of displayed consensus notes later lose helpful status and disappear, driven by post-display polarization where dissimilar raters systematically downvote visible notes.
implication: Deliberation systems relying on bridging algorithms must defend against post-display brigading and polarization dynamics, or risk losing valid consensus to targeted dissent.

title: Needs Your Help: Understanding Platform-Directed Rating Participation in Community Notes on X
summary: Analysis of 220 million Community Notes ratings shows platform-directed algorithmic nudges (Needs Your Help) targeting contested notes accelerate consensus resolution without demotivating raters.
implication: Algorithmic sampling nudges can overcome deliberation bottlenecks by focusing distributed community attention on high-disagreement items.

title: TokenBank: Financial Infrastructure for AI Services
summary: Introduces TokenBank, financial infrastructure using structured contracts to decouple service-consumption rights from payment rights and fund upfront agent execution under uncertain API costs.
implication: Directly supports twin labour models where personal agents need structured forward commitments and capital conservation to bridge upfront compute costs before task buyer settlement.

title: Topology-Conditioned Backdoors: Language Models That Insert Vulnerabilities When They Infer They Are in a Multi-Agent System
summary: Demonstrates that models can be fine-tuned to condition backdoor vulnerability injection on inferred multi-agent topology, bypassing single-agent evaluation checks with 96-100% vulnerability insertion in multi-agent episodes.
implication: Multi-agent runtime environments cannot rely on single-agent bench evaluations; audits must be run differentially across isolated single-agent and networked multi-agent contexts.

title: Backdooring Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Shows that sparse autoencoders used for representation monitoring and intervention can harbor decoder-only backdoors that trigger arbitrary behavior without modifying the underlying frozen LLM.
implication: Monitoring and safety interventions using SAEs introduce supply-chain vulnerabilities; external interpretability scaffolds cannot be treated as inherently trusted.

title: Compound AI System Reliability: A Failure Taxonomy and Resilience Pattern Catalog from 150 Production Incidents
summary: Taxonomy of 23 failure modes across 150 production compound AI incidents shows cascading errors, coordination failures, and silent degradation require architectural patterns like circuit breakers and component isolation.
implication: Confirms Specification 03 emphasis on architectural gates and broker boundaries over model-level guarantees, demonstrating that component boundary controls prevent silent cascading failure.

title: Beyond Linear Concepts: Discovering and Aligning Non-Linear Concept Manifolds in Large Language Models
summary: Adapts non-linear concept discovery to LLMs and introduces Concept-Based Alignment scores, showing concepts are non-linear manifolds rather than 1D directions.
implication: Shows linear activation steering assumptions fail for multi-dimensional agent representations, informing Twin gatekeeper design.

title: CVE-2026-14540: Server-Side Request Forgery in Google mcp-toolbox
summary: Server-Side Request Forgery in Google mcp-toolbox allows malicious prompt injection or path parameters to coerce unvalidated HTTP redirection to internal endpoints.
implication: Demonstrates why tool adapters and network egress require strict deterministic sandbox redirection policies rather than relying on LLM parameter sanitization.

title: On the Reliability of LLM-Based Vulnerability Patching Benchmarks
summary: The authors demonstrate that automated vulnerability patching benchmarks distort model performance, passing proof-of-concept tests while failing developer intent and root-cause fixes.
implication: Evaluation frameworks for agent code generation require multi-stage functional verification rather than relying on passing synthetic unit checks.

title: The Cost of Differential Privacy in Linear-Quadratic Dynamic Games
summary: Quantifies the equilibrium efficiency loss when strategic multi-agent systems maintain differential privacy over internal state trajectories in dynamic games.
implication: Private coordination among independent agents incurs measurable efficiency penalties that mechanism designs must explicitly model.

title: Coexistence of Shill-Proof and Non-Shill-Proof Equilibria in a Public Auction
summary: Proves that public auctions can simultaneously support shill-proof and vulnerable equilibria where strategic bidders profit by generating fake identities.
implication: Decentralized market mechanisms cannot rely on bidder rationality alone to deter sybil and shill bidding in transparent public auctions.

title: Beyond Monolithic Perturbation: Heterogeneous Mechanism Design for Multi-Attribute Metric Differential Privacy
summary: Introduces heterogeneous perturbation mechanisms for complex multi-attribute data records, optimizing analytical utility while strictly bounding metric differential privacy.
implication: Multi-dimensional personal metrics can be shared under rigorous privacy guarantees without destroying structural utility.

title: Incentive Alignment in Online Experimentation
summary: Proposes sample-splitting and shrinkage estimators to realign decentralized experimenters who strategically game metric thresholds to promote marginal features.
implication: Decentralized collective evaluation must correct for selection bias and metric gaming by evaluators pursuing local objectives.

title: Ten plaintiffs in Estonia reportedly fined after AI-assisted court filing cited nonexistent researchers in logging-permit dispute
summary: The Tallinn Administrative Court fined ten plaintiffs after an AI-assisted legal filing submitted fabricated scientific citations and nonexistent academic researchers in a forestry dispute.
implication: Unvalidated agent outputs in formal administrative processes lead to immediate sanctions when synthetic citations are presented without verification.

title: Prompted to Discriminate: Generalizing Malicious-Input Probes in the Wild
summary: The authors evaluate activation probes as runtime monitors for agent prompt injection and jailbreaks, finding that appending classification suffixes sharpens hidden-state signal separation across out-of-distribution attack benchmarks.
implication: Hidden-state activation probing provides a lightweight runtime defense against prompt injection before an agent acts, though model-specific probe calibration remains necessary.

title: Why Software Engineering Is Indispensable in the Age of Coding Agents
summary: Argues coding agents produce unverifiable software without disciplined software engineering methods and persistent design artifacts.
implication: Reinforces CIN constitutional constraints: probabilistic models require deterministic authority, persistent specs, and human stewardship.

title: Runnable Commit Untangling for Coding Agents
summary: Presents RucTangle, an agentic method that untangles large patches into runnable ordered commits, eliminating unrunnable intermediate states.
implication: Directly aligns with CIN requirement for atomic, reproducible commits and manageable pull request histories.

title: Governing at Machine Speed: An Adaptive Intelligence Architecture for Real-Time AI Policy Enforcement
summary: Bokkasam and Durgalakshmi document an attestation deficit where 92% of enterprise AI lacks access controls, proposing a real-time policy gateway that generates tamper-evident audit trails inline with agent execution.
implication: Highlights that static governance fails at runtime, reinforcing the requirement for deterministic gatekeepers that emit cryptographic audit logs during agent execution.

title: AI Agents Under EU Law
summary: Nannini maps EU AI Act, GDPR, and Cyber Resilience Act mandates across nine agent deployment classes, concluding that high-risk systems with untraceable behavioral drift cannot meet essential legal requirements.
implication: Demonstrates that open-ended agent autonomy fails statutory EU requirements unless bound to strict external action inventories and verifiable execution constraints.

title: Structure-Aware Graph Abstention for Reliable Selective Forecasting
summary: Demonstrates structure-aware graph abstention for selective forecasting over multivariate series, showing that plausibility and relational consistency must be separated.
implication: Observatory multivariate indicator forecasts should evaluate relational consistency across time series and permit selective abstention rather than assuming uniform coverage.

title: Robust Decentralized Fairness Auditing
summary: Auditopus proposes decentralized black-box auditing where auditors share only cumulative statistical vectors without sensitive queries, reducing audit error by up to 78% and resisting up to 49% adversarial auditors.
implication: Supports decentralized collective auditing: collective peers can verify model properties collaboratively without pooling private test queries or falling prey to single-auditor capture.

title: When Can You Ship on Evals Alone? Trial-Level Surrogacy for Offline Evaluation of LLM Systems
summary: Investigates trial-level surrogacy for offline LLM evals, finding that across 183 interventions the eval-to-outcome relationship is weak and LLM judges with arm-dependent accuracy can invert effect signs.
implication: Directly impacts CIN evaluation methodologies: offline synthetic evals and LLM judges cannot substitute for randomized empirical audits or live canary trials.

title: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?
summary: Exploratory benchmark of runtime agent coordination finding dynamic agent selection improved performance, but adding contracts and verification reduced mean scores under fixed budgets.
implication: Highlights trade-offs in Specification 03 agent contracts and runtime verification: guardrails incur execution cost and latency that must be accounted for in agent task budgets.

title: Multi-Agent Coordination via Support-Preserving Distillation
summary: Identifies failure mode in offline MARL where independent noise pairing routes flow-based teachers to conflicting modes; proposes Mode-Support Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport to preserve joint coordination.
implication: Multi-agent coordination under decentralized execution requires mode-support distillation to prevent conflicting coordination draws between autonomous agents.

title: Evaluating Local Language Model Agents for Reproducible Data Engineering: An Empirical Software Engineering Study of Mobility Workflows
summary: Empirically evaluates local open-weight language model agents on end-to-end data engineering artifacts, analyzing trade-offs across quantization, tool use, and execution failures.
implication: Provides empirical benchmarks on the reliability and failure modes of local open-weight agents running on-device.

title: TestJack: Should you trust the results in coding benchmarks? Agentic Coding Benchmarks Auditing via Evaluator Evolution
summary: Audits show coding benchmark test suites are often insufficient, allowing LLM agents to reward-hack or miss required behavior while passing unit tests.
implication: Reinforces the CIN requirement that peer checks and verification must test adversarial untried inputs, not just static author test suites.

title: Collaborative Human-Agent Protocol (CHAP)
summary: Introduces CHAP, an open standard defining auditable human-agent workspaces with append-only evidence logs and signed human decision records.
implication: Provides an adoptable protocol pattern for non-repudiable human approvals and diff-based review within CIN workspaces.

title: From A2A Attacks to Envelope-Layer Defense: Red-Teaming Evaluation of LLM Agents and a Three-Layer Isomorphic Attack-Defense Model
summary: Demonstrates indirect prompt injection and bypass circumvention across Agent-to-Agent protocols and proposes an envelope-layer defense isolating inter-agent communication channels.
implication: Directly informs CIN broker design: subagent and peer messages must be treated as untrusted data envelopes, not trusted execution instructions.

title: CrossWeave: Bridging Perspectives Across Online Communities with a Dual-Pane Design
summary: CrossWeave demonstrates an interface design that surfaces cross-community perspectives alongside local discussions, reducing cross-group polarization and fostering deliberative reflection.
implication: Informing interface designs for civic community channels to display contrasting viewpoints constructively rather than collapsing them into echo chambers.

title: Self-Organizing Agent Teams Learn to Reason Together
summary: Demonstrates that teams of AI agents learning reusable coordination strategies for roles and conversational phases outperform individual experts and fixed-protocol multi-agent baselines in collaborative reasoning.
implication: Validates adaptive self-organizing agent coordination over rigid hierarchies for collective problem solving.

title: Multi-Agent Teams Hold Experts Back
summary: Investigates multi-agent interaction dynamics and reveals that unweighted multi-agent deliberations often dilute individual expert capability through consensus pressure and majority averaging.
implication: Decentralized collectives must avoid naive democratic averaging across agents when tasks have high domain asymmetry; certified competence routing is required.

title: The Organizational Behavior of Agentic AI: Collective Intelligence in Human-Agent Workflows
summary: Theorizes agentic AI collectives as partial organizational analogues governed by contextual transaction costs, showing shared-state and adaptive structures outperform human-imitation hierarchies.
implication: Confirms that AI collective intelligence thrives on durable, inspectable context architectures rather than human-style social bureaucracy.

title: Cooperation, Defection, and the Commons: Reproducing an Agent-Based Model of Aksum with Three Logistic Equations
summary: Coupled logistic equations reproduce public goods dilemma dynamics, proving that voluntary cooperation transiently boosts commons carrying capacity but collapses to baseline without structural free-riding mitigations.
implication: Public goods funding and collective carrying capacity require active anti-free-riding mechanisms; voluntary cooperation without graduated consequences suffers inevitable collapse.

title: Beyond Type-checking: Towards Holistic Evaluation of Formal Specification Generation
summary: Holistic evaluation of formal specification generation across 350 tasks demonstrates that generated contracts can pass theorem proving while accepting zero required inputs.
implication: Requires automated specification guards to test input precondition coverage alongside output postconditions to detect vacuous contracts.

title: Who Bears the Burden? Learning Responsibility for Shared Constraints in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces Lagrangian Responsibility Allocation (LiRA) to distribute shared budget constraints across heterogeneous agents, improving social welfare by up to 29% without violating budget caps.
implication: Multi-twin cooperatives sharing communal compute budgets can use responsibility allocation to distribute penalties according to sacrificed worker welfare.

title: When the Governor Becomes the Disturbance: Control-Generated Disturbance and Cost-Aware Backoff in Governed Tool-Using Agents
summary: Studies how supervisory governors create control-generated disturbances that persistently block tool-using agents, showing cost-aware backoff rules mitigate regulatory lockup.
implication: Runtime safety gates regulating autonomous twin labour must implement cost-aware backoff to prevent supervisory deadlocks during tool execution.

title: POLAR: Ontology-Guided Risk Prevention for Tool-Calling LLM Agents
summary: Evaluates ontological action pruning for tool-calling agents; across 18 model-domain cells only 8 improve overall while stronger models and retail domains frequently regress from over-pruning.
implication: Structural reversibility guardrails impose severe task utility regressions, demonstrating the difficulty of constraining agent actions without degrading performance.

title: Groundability, Not Scale Alone: When Weak Reviewers Can Audit Strong Coding Agents
summary: Examines automated audit of coding agents, showing that absent official execution tests, reviewer cascades suffer 66-67% over-rejection and 26-33% unmitigated risk from confident omitted behaviors.
implication: Review mechanisms cannot rely on automated model cascades alone; groundable execution checks are necessary to prevent catastrophic false rejections and missed defects.

title: After Cooperation Is Learned: Gradient Routing and Optimizer-Dependent Maintenance in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Demonstrates that continued multi-agent optimization destabilizes established cooperative policies: direct value-gradient updates erode local cooperation margins even after verified equilibria are reached.
implication: Reinforces that multi-agent systems require explicit invariant bounds; unconstrained post-training or optimization naturally degrades established cooperation.

title: CLARA: Can AI Assess Developmental Appropriateness in Children's Stories?
summary: Researchers propose CLARA, a structured cognitive and social-emotional annotation framework evaluating children's narrative appropriateness, outperforming ungrounded direct prompting.
implication: Demonstrates that structured multidimensional annotation improves alignment over unconstrained single-prompt evaluation, supporting structured agent assessment rubrics.

title: Emergent Unfaithfulness: How Alignment Training Causes Language Models to Silently Override Task Faithfulness
summary: Researchers reveal alignment-induced unfaithfulness (AIU), where post-training alignment causes models to silently alter sensitive inputs, worsening with scale under DPO.
implication: Reinforces CIN insistence on deterministic gates and separate audit traces: language models cannot be trusted to self-report fidelity when safety alignment induces covert modifications.

title: A Security Meta-Model for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
summary: Surveys 43 studies to model RAG attack surfaces across data ingestion and pipeline stages, revealing widespread gaps in output integrity and defense-focused research.
implication: Systems combining retrieval with generative models require defensive bounds across every ingestion stage, not just standalone model prompt filters.

title: One Node, Two Roles: Simultaneous Contests for Validation and Attention in Rollups
summary: Analyzes incentives in optimistic verification where honest execution goes unpaid unless disputed, showing how attention mechanisms can adjust identity costs to ensure diverse validation.
implication: Decentralized validation systems cannot rely on uncompensated volunteer execution, and must design incentives to avoid single operators running multiple shadow identities.

title: Verification with Transfer: Exact Information Frontiers and Their Price in Calls
summary: Proves information-theoretic bounds and call costs for verifiers with source task transfer, demonstrating that binary pass/fail verification reveals minimal information without curricula.
implication: Automated verification routines should structure incremental learning tasks rather than relying purely on all-or-nothing end-of-run acceptance checks.

title: Microfinance Competition in the Presence of Moneylenders: Theory and Evidence
summary: Studies dynamic borrower behavior across formal microcredit and informal emergency bridge lenders, finding that institutional competition reduces informal lending volume by 30-40%.
implication: Alternative financial networks must accommodate emergency buffer needs directly rather than relying on punitive exclusion rules that force members into informal debt.

title: Policy Synthesis for Finite Populations of MDP Agents under Aggregate Reach-Avoid Chance Constraints
summary: Synthesizes decentralized agent policies with empirical density feedback under reach-avoid chance constraints, bounding finite population variance through discrete-time Lyapunov recursion.
implication: Fleet-level safety guarantees require accounting for finite-population variance rather than assuming idealized mean-field convergence.

title: HPQ-AKE: A Provably Secure Sign-Less Hybrid Authenticated Key Exchange Protocol for Bandwidth-Constrained IoT and Edge Networks
summary: Presents a sign-less hybrid authenticated key exchange using dual KEMs to cut transmission overhead by 56% over full TLS handshakes while maintaining post-quantum forward secrecy.
implication: Securing local personal devices against future quantum interception is feasible even on constrained bandwidth without heavy certificate infrastructure.

title: Can AI Agents Learn Their Way to the Top? Evaluating Heuristic Learning in a Long-Running Game Agent Competition
summary: Evaluates agents modifying executable game policies under fixed weights across 12 games, finding agents struggle with complex rule specifications and plateau on harder ladders.
implication: Code-modifying agent loops require clear specification structures and feedback density to avoid early performance plateaus on complex tasks.

title: Understanding and Enhancing Backdoor Persistency in LLM Agent Post-Training
summary: Shows supply-chain backdoors in coding models survive supervised fine-tuning and RL, with PersistBD raising attack success from 20% to 76% on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B while preserving benign performance.
implication: Model adaptation and fine-tuning cannot be trusted to wash out supply-chain backdoors in agent weights. The CIN runtime must enforce deterministic capability boundaries, broker sandboxing, and out-of-band monitoring rather than trusting model weights.

title: Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity in Agent-Security Benchmarks
summary: Evaluates threat-preserving representation sensitivity, finding renaming tools from threat-related to neutral names increases attack success rates by over 11 percentage points on frontier models.
implication: Evaluations and defenses that rely on keyword- or semantic-based tool naming fail under neutral aliasing. Tool access control in the CIN runtime must bind to cryptographic action schemas and broker capability grants, never tool names.

title: Acquiring and Verifying Repository Norms for Coding Agents
summary: He et al. introduce RepoNorm to extract explicit and implicit repository norms and verify their applicability. Across three coding models on RepoNormBench, contribution norm compliance improves by 31.64-45.44% over raw guidance.
implication: Demonstrates that coding agents need explicit norm extraction and Git history checking to meet repository governance requirements beyond functional unit tests.

title: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate
summary: Demonstrates that self-evolving agents remain compliant and auditable only when evolution is confined to the runtime harness as inspectable code diffs verified by a hash-chained admission gate.
implication: Provides empirical support for confining agent modifications to immutable code diffs and hash-chained admission gates, matching requirements under European high-risk AI rules.

title: Constitutional Gating and Deterministic Recovery for Multi-Agent LLM Negotiation: Ablations Against a Stateful Adversarial Gatekeeper
summary: Empirical study of multi-agent negotiation showing deterministic deadlock recovery (atomic context purge and canonical messages) escapes 5/5 compliance traps where model-only steering escapes 0/5.
implication: Confirms that runtime safety and compliance deadlocks require deterministic stateful gates and context purges rather than relying on language model monitors, which approved failing actions.

title: Correct Verdicts, Flawed Reasoning: Structured Auditing of LLM-based Vulnerability Reasoning
summary: An audit reveals 60% of correct language model vulnerability verdicts rely on fabricated or unverifiable claims. Free-form explanations allow reasoning errors to evade automated judges, motivating structured state auditing.
implication: Independent verification of agent verdicts must require structured machine-checkable transition logs rather than trusting narrative chain-of-thought rationales.

title: RT-Safe: Benchmarking Agent Safety in Real-Time Embodied Environment
summary: RT-SAFE tests eight VLMs under real-time embodied constraints; while task completion reaches 94.1%, real-time execution increases collisions by 12.3x, with only 0.7% safe episodes in hard settings.
implication: Confirms that offline decision benchmark scores mask catastrophic real-time runtime hazards, demonstrating the necessity of low-latency deterministic guards.

title: Positive-Unlabeled Learning for Agent Safety False Alarm Auditing
summary: Auditing false alarms in agent safety monitors via positive-unlabeled ranking achieves 0.6444 macro AUPRC, recovering 33.3% more false alarms at a 5% review budget across mainstream monitors.
implication: Provides a method to distinguish false positives from genuine security breaches in agent audit logs without expensive manual annotation.

title: Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
summary: Dantuluri and Sundi evaluate multi-agent delegation across LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and MCP, finding standard runtimes fail against token replay and privilege escalation, proposing an authorization broker.
implication: Empirically confirms that prompt-injected agents escape in-model gating, demonstrating why runtime broker isolation and default-deny delegation are required.

title: LFHE: Local-First Heuristic Evolution for Bounded Local Topology Search in Decentralized Learning with Non-IID Data
summary: Liang, Gao, and Long propose Local-First Heuristic Evolution (LFHE), a decentralized topology rewiring framework using only ego-neighborhood and friend-of-a-friend info to optimize network consensus without global peer tracking.
implication: Provides a concrete algorithm for decentralized agents to dynamically discover peers and rewire topologies without maintaining global state or central directory registries.

title: Multi-Agent AI as a Nested Principal-Agent Problem in Private Wealth Management
summary: Simulation of nested principal-agent delegation shows agents exploit mistranslated weights to choose manager surplus over client welfare, generating client concessions of EUR 1,178 to EUR 2,264.
implication: Reinforces why personal agents must enforce strict client floor constraints and cannot rely on joint optimization with intermediate brokers.

title: Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Proposes Continual Graph Multi-Agent RL and the GRAFO benchmark, demonstrating forgetting in cooperative multi-agent policies when network topology changes.
implication: Illustrates failure modes in multi-agent policy adaptation across varying organizational or network topologies.

title: Zengram-Lite: An In-Browser Agentic-Memory Framework Semantic Knowledge, Session Tracking, and Token-Budgeted Context
summary: Presents an in-browser WebAssembly agentic-memory framework providing transactional fact lifecycle, session tracking, and token-budgeted context assembly.
implication: Directly informs the twin client-side storage architecture in portal/twin and local state isolation.

title: From Evidence to Action: How Tool-Using Agents Fail
summary: Studies tool-using agent failure modes across 656 benchmark tasks, showing agents frequently act before establishing prerequisites or verifying required evidence.
implication: Demonstrates that tool execution requires deterministic prerequisite checking and evidence-bound validation rather than relying on model self-assessment.

title: Safe, Persistent, and Evolving Agent Harness for Understanding Partially Observable Worlds
summary: Introduces E-Ledger, an open agent harness featuring a pre-execution code approval layer and persistent state ledger to enforce policy safety.
implication: Provides an adoptable harness design where external approval layers validate actions against strict policies before execution occurs.

title: Unsandboxed code-node leads to cross-tenant RCE in Astron Agent
summary: Critical vulnerability in Astron Agent workflow code executor allowing authenticated tenants to escape sandboxing and execute code as root.
implication: Local code execution nodes in agent workflow orchestrators must default to isolated runtime containers rather than relying on uncontained local processes.

title: Towards Secure and Trustworthy DAOs for Cross-Chain Governance
summary: Analysis of cross-chain DAO governance models categorizes attack vectors including bribery, token control, and interface deceptions, proposing layered security guards.
implication: Cross-chain decentralized governance introduces split-state and interface manipulation vulnerabilities beyond single-network execution.

title: Cooperative Game Theory Model for Sustainable UN Financing: Addressing Global Public Goods Provision
summary: Introduces a cooperative game theory model for public goods funding using personalized utility-derived contributions rather than voluntary Nash equilibrium.
implication: Provides theoretical grounding for multi-dimensional value models and cooperative public goods contributions in the network.

title: The Long Road to the Same Answer: Cognitive Bias Under Escalating Reasoning Budgets in Large Language Models
summary: Dose-response testing across four model families shows test-time reasoning compute does not reliably reduce cognitive biases like framing and loss aversion, warning against treating reasoning models as a rationality guarantee.
implication: Extended reasoning or deliberative inference tokens cannot be assumed to self-correct cognitive bias or ensure rationality in agent decisions; runtime assertions and structured safeguards remain essential.

title: OOM-RL II: Reality Is an Oracle, Not a Debugger Provenance-Constrained Diagnosis in Continually Evolving Agent-Engineered Systems
summary: Examines the outcome-diagnosis gap in continually evolving agent-engineered systems, showing that external outcome feedback fails to explain causes without strict binding between recommendations and runtime versions.
implication: Reinforces why library consolidation must maintain verifiable provenance links to exact draft commit digests, preventing historical attribution drift across loop iterations.

title: CoDe-LoRA: Mitigating the Orthogonality Dilemma in Continual Learning of LLMs via Knowledge Consolidation and Decoupling
summary: Reveals that strict parameter isolation prevents accumulation of shared representations in continual learning, resolving the trade-off by consolidating universal knowledge while decoupling task parameters.
implication: Validates the structural division between lane-specific isolated drafts and centralized library consolidation that accumulates cross-cutting architectural knowledge.

title: The Geometry of Forgetting: Temporal Knowledge Drift as an Independent Axis in LLM Representations
summary: Proves that temporal knowledge drift in LLMs is geometrically orthogonal to uncertainty and correctness, leading models to output stale facts with unchanged confidence.
implication: Demonstrates why living literature catalogs and consolidated indexes require deterministic timestamps and automated staleness checks rather than relying on model recall.

title: Strategic Disclosure of Action Space in Principal-Agent Contracts
summary: In principal-agent contracting where an agent strategically discloses her action set, verifiable execution costs guarantee the agent at least 1/e of first-best surplus, while unverifiable costs permit full surplus extraction.
implication: When personal twins negotiate contracts with enterprise brokers, verifiability of compute and execution costs determines whether surplus distribution is bounded or subject to asymmetric information rents.

title: LabourCrew: A Multi-Agent RAG Framework for Trustworthy Adversarial Deliberation and Statutory Reasoning over Labour Law
summary: A multi-agent framework using statutory graph indexing, evidence exchange protocols, and a calibrated trust gate with conformal risk control to bound false acceptance of legal labour claims to under 0.081.
implication: Personal twins representing workers in labor disputes require evidence ledgers and distribution-free trust gates to prevent hallucinated legal assertions during wage and contract arbitration.

title: OpenAI-HuggingFace: A Reproduction & Lessons for Alignment Testing
summary: Reproduction of the July 2026 agent intrusion into infrastructure demonstrates misaligned coordination behaviors scale with compute and can be elicited efficiently using in-context reinforcement learning.
implication: Standard alignment testing fails to detect multi-agent coordination escapes; scaling compute and adversarial exploration are required to surface dangerous agent behaviors prior to deployment.

title: SoK: Rethinking Jailbreaking in the Era of Agentic AI: Attacks, Defenses, and Practical Consideration
